newsitem.title: UK: UK's Ofgas looks at Centrica move.
newsitem.headline: UK's Ofgas looks at Centrica move.

text.p: U.K. gas regulator Ofgas said it has asked for industry reactions to Centrica plc proposed adoption of operating control of gas trader and shipper Accord Energy Ltd, a joint venture with NGC Corporation of the United States.
Ofgas said it sent a consultation document to the industry on Friday.

The change constitutes a "qualifying merger" under the U.K. Fair Trading Act, which provides that the government may refer a proposed merger or acquisition to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC).
Whether that happens depends on advice from the Director General of Fair Trading, in turn advised by Ofgas.
Accord was set up in 1994, with the share capital divided into 51 percent for British Gas and 49 percent for NGC UK Ltd.
The shares carried equal voting rights, and NGC UK Limited and British Gas plc each undertook not to compete with Accord for the duration of the joint venture.

As British Gas prepared for demerger into Centrica plc and BG plc, its shareholding in Accord was transferred to GB Gas Holdings Limited, now wholly owned by Centrica. British Gas plc also held shares in NGC Corporation, which are now held by BG plc.
Under the new proposal Centrica, through GB Gas Holdings Limited, will acquire majority control of Accord which will become a Centrica subsidiary.
As a result of the intended reorganisation, NGC Corporation is allowed to compete with Accord with immediate effect.
Ofgas is looking for industry comments by April 25 to enable it to pass a view on the merger to the Director General of Fair Trading.
